units.text: The stop statement terminates execution of test components, a test case or a test control.
stop
The stop statement terminates execution in different ways depending on the context in which it is executed.
When executed in a control behaviour, it terminates the execution of the control component.
When invoked in a test case, altstep or function that are executed on a test component, it terminates the relevant test component.
NOTE: The semantics of a stop statement that terminates a test component is identical to the stop component operation self.stop (see clause 21.3.3).
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
The return statement terminates execution of functions or altsteps.
return [ Expression | TemplateInstance ]
The return statement terminates execution of a function or altstep and returns control to the point from which the function or altstep was called.
When used in functions, a return statement may be optionally associated with a return value or template.
TTCN-3 allows optional statement blocks that may follow altstep calls within alt statements.
If there is a statement block, the return statement returns control to the beginning of this statement block and the statement block is executed before the alt statement is left.
If there is no statement block, test execution continues with the first statement following the alt statement.
The return value or template is first evaluated before returning.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16, the following restrictions apply:
a) The return statement shall not be present in testcase definitions.
The log statement provides the means to write logging information to some logging device.
The information that can be logged is summarized in table 18.
Table 18: TTCN-3 language elements that can be logged
Used in a log statement: module parameter identifier; What is logged: actual value
Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.
Used in a log statement: data constant identifier; What is logged: actual value
Used in a log statement: template instance; What is logged: actual template or field values and matching symbols
Used in a log statement: variable identifier; What is logged: actual value or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: See notes 3 and 4.

Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.
Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.
Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.
Used in a log statement: checkstate operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.
Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.
Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.
Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.
Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.
Used in a log statement: read operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: See clause 23.4.
Used in a log statement: match operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.
Used in a log statement: valueof operation; What is logged: return value
Used in a log statement: getverdict operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: none, pass, inconc, or fail.
Used in a log statement: predefined functions; What is logged: return value; Comment: See annex C.
Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.
Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.
Used in a log statement; What is logged; Comment

**Used in a log statement** **What is logged** **Comment** formal parameter identifier see comment column Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting.

In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.
NOTE 1: Actual value/actual template is the value/template at the moment of the execution of the log statement.
NOTE 2: The type of the logged value is tool dependent.
NOTE 3: In case of array identifiers without array element specification, actual values and for component references names of all array elements shall be logged.
NOTE 4: The string "UNINITIALIZED" is logged only if the log item is unbound (uninitialized).
NOTE 5: Component states that can be logged are: Inactive, Running, Stopped and Killed (for further details see annex F).
NOTE 6: Port states that can be logged are: Started and Stopped (for further details see annex F).
NOTE 7: Default states that can be logged are: Activated and Deactivated.
NOTE 8: Timer states that can be logged are: Inactive, Running and Expired (for further details see annex F).
NOTE 9: As the logging of the fields of structured values and templates is not standardized, tools supplied by different vendors may differ in the logged information.
log "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")"
The log statement provides the means to write one or more log items to some logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the statement is used.
Items to be logged shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the log statement.
Log items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such log items.
It is strongly recommended that the execution of the log statement has no effect on the test behaviour.

In particular, functions used in a log statement should not (explicitly or implicitly) change component variable values, port or timer status, and should not change the value of any of its inout or out parameters.
NOTE: It is outside the scope of the present document to define complex logging and trace capabilities which may be tool dependent.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
A break statement causes the exit from a loop, from an altstep or from an alt or interleave statement.
break

Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.
NOTE 1: Actual value/actual template is the value/template at the moment of the execution of the log statement.
NOTE 2: The type of the logged value is tool dependent.
NOTE 3: In case of array identifiers without array element specification, actual values and for component references names of all array elements shall be logged.
NOTE 4: The string "UNINITIALIZED" is logged only if the log item is unbound (uninitialized).
NOTE 5: Component states that can be logged are: Inactive, Running, Stopped and Killed (for further details see annex F).
NOTE 6: Port states that can be logged are: Started and Stopped (for further details see annex F).
NOTE 7: Default states that can be logged are: Activated and Deactivated.
NOTE 8: Timer states that can be logged are: Inactive, Running and Expired (for further details see annex F).
NOTE 9: As the logging of the fields of structured values and templates is not standardized, tools supplied by different vendors may differ in the logged information.
Used in a log statement; What is logged; Comment
On executing a break statement the innermost, currently executed loop, alt statement or interleave statement is left.
Execution continues with the statement following the construct which is left.
Using break outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) or an alternative of an alt or interleave statement shall cause an error.
Altsteps are always executed within a surrounding alt statement.
If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep (see clause 16.2.1) ends with a break statement, the altstep and the surrounding alt statement are left.
Execution continues with the statement following the surrounding alt statement.
NOTE: TTCN-3 allows optional statement blocks that may follow altstep calls within alt statements.
These statement blocks are not executed when the altstep is left by executing a break statement.
A return statement has to be used, if such an optional statement block has to be executed (see clause 19.10).
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
A continue statement causes the start of the next iteration of a loop.
continue
On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.
Using continue outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) shall cause an error.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
Statement blocks can be used like basic program statements to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.
The declarations and statements in a statement block are executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially.
"{" { LocalDefinition | Statement } "}"
A statement block defines a local scope unit.
Scoping rules for TTCN-3 are defined in clause 5.2.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
